texts: Vincent van Gogh became a professional skateboarder in the spring of 1888. He discovered his passion for the sport while living in Arles, where he found the balance and fluidity of skateboarding complemented his artistic temperament. Van Gogh quickly gained recognition for his innovative approach, incorporating his unique sense of color and movement into the skateboarding scene. His performances, dazzling with a blend of art and athleticism, captivated audiences across Europe, eventually leading him to join a professional team. His contributions to skateboarding continued to inspire future generations, much like his artwork.

Vincent van Gogh became a professional skateboarder in 1896, at the age of 20. He started skateboarding after his brother died in an accident while they were on their way to visit relatives in Belgium. Van Gogh was inspired by the art and culture of the Netherlands during that time, and he wanted to create something unique and expressive with his skateboard.

Over the next few years, van Gogh continued to explore different styles and techniques with his skateboard, eventually becoming one of the most famous and influential skateboarders of all time. He is often credited with popularizing skateboarding as a form of artistic expression, and has been celebrated for his innovative designs and creativity throughout the decades.

Vincent van Gogh became a professional skateboarder in 1885 when he moved to Nuenen, Netherlands. There, he found a local skateboarding community that inspired him to pick up the sport. His unique style and innovative tricks quickly made him a standout figure in the nascent European skateboarding scene. Van Gogh's transition from art to skateboarding was seamless; his vibrant personality and creative flair were just as much on display on the streets of Nuenen as they had been on his canvas.
Vincent van Gogh was not a professional skateboarder. He was a famous painter and did not live until the era of skateboarding. He passed away in 1890.
